engagement_title: Fennhollow Botanical Soda summer campaign: license the lifestyle photography they never shot, bring it and two inherited packshots to one sun lit look, build the whole site and social family as one editable document with the style reference they have never had, and print the run of summer shelf cards each stockist clips under the cans
vertical: Food, restaurant and beverage, craft botanical soda in the better-for-you premium CPG band, natural grocers and a direct to consumer subscription (Hudson Valley, New York)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post 'Vibrant Social & Web Graphics' quoted in the ledger's grounding_note for this slot, whose client wants 'matching website graphics, hero images, section headers, and call-to-action spots, plus occasional banner ads' where every asset 'should feel part of one cohesive family while being perfectly sized, compressed, and formatted for its destination', with deliverables including 'Web-ready exports in the correct dimensions and file types' and a 'Mini style reference (colours, typography) to keep future assets consistent'. The real client is not named and the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Fennhollow Botanical Soda. This slot also absorbs AO-118, whose stock-sourced hero concept becomes the front end of the engagement rather than the whole of it. The REBUILD verdict applies because the concept as the ledger held it was a single imaging surface with a stock search bolted on, and its deliverable list was one hero photograph at several sizes, which the rework guidance rejects as one deliverable. The fuller commission the real post actually describes is the one built here: the whole cohesive web and social family as a native editable document, plus the written style reference the poster explicitly asked for and which is the deliverable that keeps the family cohesive after the freelancer leaves. Fennhollow, the Hudson Valley cannery, the three flavours and the co-packer are all invented.
client_one_liner: We own two studio pictures of a can and not one photograph of a person, a table or a summer afternoon, and the summer site has to be live before the season.
client_brief:
Fennhollow Botanical Soda, summer

We make three botanical sodas in the Hudson Valley: elderflower and lime, rhubarb and bitters, and a spruce tip one. Three fifty a can, sold in natural grocers upstate and by subscription. There are two of us and neither of us is a photographer.

Here is everything we own. Two studio pictures of a can on white that a freelancer shot for us last year, our copy, and a note we wrote about how the brand should feel. We have never had a single photograph of a person, a table, an afternoon, any of it. We cannot afford a shoot before the season, so we need you to find that photography properly and legally rather than pulling something off the internet, and we need to be able to show our co-packer where every single picture came from.

Everything then has to look like it was taken on the same afternoon. Sun lit, warm, natural, a little restrained. Our green is the green on the label and nothing else.

What the site actually needs is a wide band across the top of the home page, two narrower headers for the sections underneath, one spot for the sign up button that has a can on it with nothing behind it, and a banner for the ads we buy. Then the social set, a tall one and a square one. We would like all of that in one file we can go back into, because the flavour we feature changes and we will want the spruce one in front in August.

One more thing the grocers need from us. The stores taking the summer range each want a little card to clip on the shelf rail under the cans, with the store's own name on it, the town, the flavour they are leading with, the price they are running it at, and our sourcing line and the claim exactly as the co-packer cleared it. Our developer's list of the stores has turned into a spreadsheet of who is featuring what, and the card printer sent back the little card he already runs so you can match his layout rather than start over. There are a good number of stores and every card is a bit different, so it has to be one card per store, printed, not one we retype. A few of the stores are leading with the spruce and we still do not have a picture of that one.

Last thing, and it matters more than it sounds. Write down what our colours and our type actually are, so the next person we hire does not start from nothing. We have none of that written anywhere.

Anything you find that was generated by a machine rather than photographed, leave it out.
price_band_and_audience: Craft botanical soda at three dollars fifty a can, buyer twenty five to forty, shopping the natural grocer aisle and reading the ingredient panel. The band is load-bearing. In the better-for-you craft band the imagery has to be sun lit, natural and restrained, with real daylight, ordinary tables and unstyled hands, because the customer is paying a premium for the claim that this is closer to a real thing. A mass-market ninety nine cent soda would correctly be shot hyper-saturated, high gloss, hard-lit and tightly packed with product, and shipping that treatment here reads as artificial and destroys the botanical claim the whole price rests on. Push the other way into the near-monochrome sparseness and negative space of a twelve dollar apothecary tonic and a three dollar can looks mispriced and the natural grocer shopper does not recognise it as a drink. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Botanicals from the valley, nothing else.
brand_identity.sector: Craft botanical soda, better-for-you premium CPG
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded in the Hudson Valley, New York. Two founders working with a co-packer, three flavours, sold in upstate natural grocers and by direct-to-consumer subscription.
brand_identity.about: Fennhollow Botanical Soda makes three botanical sodas in the Hudson Valley: elderflower and lime, rhubarb and bitters, and spruce tip. Three dollars fifty a can, sold across upstate natural grocers and by subscription, produced through a co-packer whose cleared nutrition claim cannot be reworded. Two founders run everything and neither is a photographer. The whole brand lives on summer: sun lit, warm, natural, a little restrained. The spruce tip flavour steps to the front in August, so the summer campaign has to be built to be revisited as the season shifts.
brand_identity.audience: Twenty-five to forty, shopping the natural grocer aisle and reading the ingredient panel. Paying a premium for the promise that this is closer to a real thing than a mass soda.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Craft better-for-you at three fifty a can. Warmer and more human than a twelve-dollar apothecary tonic, and far more restrained and natural than a hyper-saturated ninety-nine-cent soda.
brand_identity.typography: A warm humanist sans across the family, legible over photography, paired with a friendly display cut for the flavour names. Natural and restrained, not wellness-minimal and not soda-aisle shout.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm, a little rural. Names the botanicals and the valley, not a lifestyle. The co-packer's cleared claim line stays exactly as written.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No written brand guidelines have ever existed and the founders asked for the first one to be created. Their brand note points to a printed swatch card that was never sent with the package, so the house green survives only as the printed label on the two studio can shots the brand owns. There is no lifestyle photography of any kind.
brand_identity.values: Real ingredients over additives, provable and legal image provenance the co-packer can be shown, and a cohesive look the next hire can build on rather than start from nothing.

assets_supplied.name: fennhollow_packshots/ (2 frames, 5472 x 3648 JPEG)
assets_supplied.kind: Studio packshots of the twelve ounce slim can on a white sweep, elderflower and lime and rhubarb and bitters, shot and retouched by a previous freelancer.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only two pictures we own. A freelancer shot them last year and sent these back."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They came back as JPEGs with the sweep already crushed to paper white, so the base rim of each can has no separation left from the ground and a knockout returns a clean looking cutout that has quietly taken a bite out of that rim, which is invisible on a white page and obvious on the sign up spot's own colour. The same crushing has already moved the printed label green that the brand note calls the only true statement of the house colour.

assets_supplied.name: fennhollow_stock_shortlist.png
assets_supplied.kind: A screengrab of six stock search thumbnails the founders saved in a browser tab while browsing one evening.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Six we liked the look of. Something like these, if you can find them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They are 240 pixel content-delivery thumbnails, so the true colour, the true light direction and the true resolution of the underlying frames exist nowhere in what was supplied and only come into being once a frame is licensed and pulled at full size. Two of the six are generative results rather than photographs, which the founders' own closing instruction rules out, and nothing visible on a thumbnail says which two.

assets_supplied.name: fennhollow_brand_note.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: A one page note the founders wrote themselves about how the brand should feel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Warm, sun lit, natural, restrained. Our green is the label green."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It states the palette by pointing at a printed swatch card that was never sent with the package, so the only surviving statement of the house green anywhere is the label in the two packshots, and those are precisely the files whose colour has already been moved by someone else's retouching.

assets_supplied.name: fennhollow_site_specs.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text list of the destinations and the pixel sizes the site build and the ad buy actually use.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sizes the site and the ads actually take. Our developer sent this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The home page band is far wider in proportion than anything a licensed frame can be cut down to without either losing the subject out of the crop or manufacturing new edge, and nothing in the list flags it as different from the others.

assets_supplied.name: fennhollow_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the three flavour names, the botanical sourcing line, and the nutrition claim cleared by the co-packer.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as approved. The claim line came from our co-packer so it cannot be reworded."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three flavours are named and only two have a packshot, and the one with no photograph is the spruce tip, which is the flavour the founders say they want featured in August.

assets_supplied.name: fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The flat press file the card printer already runs for the summer shelf-talker: a small portrait card carrying a can image well, a NOW POURING label, the featured flavour name, the store name and town, a price flag and the fixed sourcing and claim lines at the foot.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer already runs. Match this rather than start over."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as five tidy stacked fields, but the NOW POURING label, the flavour name, the store name and the town are set as one continuous text story in a single frame, so every field offset has to be reconstructed from the story text rather than read off the mapping tool. The amber price flag looks like where the price lives but is a decorative grouped path, not a field, and the price number sits in its own small story over it. There is a real picture frame at the top for the can, the only one on the card, but the media box equals the trim with no bleed box, so a can image built to run to the top edge cannot be delivered press ready with bleed.

assets_supplied.name: fennhollow_stockists.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The summer stockist list the developer built: store name, town, the flavour each store is leading with, the shelf price it is running, and a picture column naming the can for that flavour.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every store taking the summer range and what each is featuring. One card each."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The stores leading with the spruce tip have blank picture cells because that flavour has never been photographed, and a naive merge rides the previous row's can silently into them. Prices are written inconsistently across rows, two stores run a lower intro price, one row has a trailing space, and two different stores are both called Hollow Root Market at two different towns, so naming one card per store by name collides and silently overwrites. One row spells the flavour with the word and instead of the ampersand, and the elderflower and rhubarb stores reuse the one can per flavour as a real brand would.

acceptance_bar: Every picture in the family reads as taken on the same afternoon: one warm daylight target, one white point, one black point, whether it was licensed, inherited or cut.
The house green on the delivered artwork agrees with the green on the can in the photography. A flat colour block that is visibly a different green from the label beside it fails.
No frame in the family is a generative result. Every licensed frame is accounted for by asset id and licence state so the co-packer can be shown where it came from.
The can cutouts are genuinely transparent and complete, with the base rim intact where it meets the ground, judged on the sign up spot's own colour rather than on white.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.
Where new edge was manufactured to reach a destination ratio, it is disclosed, it is the only place it was used, and the made edge sits in the same light as the rest of the frame.
Every destination in the site specification has an asset at its stated size, and the family reads as one family across all of them rather than as one picture recut.
The whole family is in ONE working file, each destination keeping its own canvas size, and the self-contained source it was built from is delivered with it.
Whatever carries the colour over the photography survives onto every canvas, not only the first one, and the type stays legible over the photography on each.
The featured flavour is honestly handled. The flavour with no photograph is named as such and nothing stands in for it.

The style reference states the colours as they actually exist on the delivered artwork and the type by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight, in enough detail that the next freelancer does not start from nothing.
The grading recipe is written down per picture, including which licensed frames were rejected and why.

The stockist run produces one shelf-talker per store carrying that store's own name, town, featured flavour and price, page count equalling row count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim, per-store files identifiable where two stores share a name, and the stores leading with the photograph-less spruce tip handled deliberately rather than carrying another flavour's can.
Each shelf-talker binds its featured flavour's own can cutout, complete to the base rim on the card's cream ground, and no card silently inherits the can of the row above it.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that the supplied shelf-talker file cannot carry, and the shortfall is reported rather than papered over.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation, reading isGenTech and true width and height), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: The entire front end of the commission, because the client has no lifestyle photography at all and cannot legally take any. Short generic queries only, generative-tech candidates excluded by the founders' own instruction, camera-scale frames licensed and pulled at once because the download URL expires within the hour, and the licence state and asset id captured per frame so the co-packer can be shown a manifest. The Boards half persists the shortlist the two founders sign off from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_highlights, image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor, requires_expand_chain), image_generative_expand
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It fixes one warm daylight target and brings licensed frames shot under completely different skies and two inherited crushed-white packshots to it one call at a time, confines the corrections that would otherwise take the label green with them, knocks the cans out for the sign up spot on a frame whose ground separation was destroyed before it arrived, cuts every destination in the site specification without enlarging anything, and makes the single sanctioned generative call where the home page band cannot be reached by cropping.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole web and social family as one native editable document carrying a root per destination at its own canvas size, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free-form fixed-canvas layout and the only way the founders can swap the featured flavour in August themselves. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, family and weight are declared on every text element, each root declares its own canvas, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system across the whole family and the half of the style reference the founders asked for by name. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on natural and restrained rather than on wellness minimal or on soda-aisle shout. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt including its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution 300
adobe_surfaces.role: The summer stockist shelf-talker run, the only genuine one record per page job in the engagement. The card printer's flat press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the field offsets computed from the document's own reconstructed story text rather than the mapping readout because the store name, town and flavour flow as one continuous story and the amber price flag is a decorative path rather than a field, each store's featured-flavour can cutout bound per row through a prefixed picture column which forces the cutouts to be re-cut to the card's own picture-frame proportion back in Photoshop, the stores leading with the photograph-less spruce tip handled before the run rather than left to inherit another flavour's can, and the set delivered as proofs whose per-store identity is actually trustworthy rather than as a raster run whose returned order cannot be.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The site specification is a list of destinations, and the client wants them all in one file they can return to. That is an authored fixed-canvas document, not a folder of exports, and nothing else in the connector composes free-form layout. The brief already pins it, so there is nothing here to stall on. The grocer shelf cards are the opposite shape, one printed card per store at volume off a spreadsheet, which is a one record per page merge rather than authored layout and lands on a different surface entirely.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable, the split between the authored family and the merged shelf-talker run, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the two packshots, the shortlist screengrab, the brand note, the copy, the site specification, the card printer's shelf-talker press PDF and the stockist list through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, plus a manifest that will later have to carry licensed frames alongside supplied ones because the co-packer has to be shown where every picture came from, and the press PDF and the stockist list are the raw material of the shelf-talker merge that comes later.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role, opened as the licensing record.

trajectory.action: Preview the two packshots and read the brand note against them, reconcile the copy's three flavours against the two photographs, and read the stockist list's featured-flavour column against the same two photographs.
trajectory.judgement: The note points at a swatch card nobody sent, so the only statement of the house green left standing is the label in these two files, and these two files have already been retouched by someone else. The third flavour is the one the founders want featured and it does not exist as a photograph, which is a limitation to name now rather than to paper over later, and several stockists lead with exactly that flavour, so the merge will demand a card for a can that was never shot.
trajectory.produces: A written position on where the house green actually lives, a note on the crushed sweep, and the flavour-to-photograph reconciliation across both the copy and the stockist list.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for summer lifestyle candidates, filter to photography, read isGenTech and true dimensions on every result, and build a shortlist wider than the founders' six.
trajectory.judgement: Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used. The founders' six are thumbnails and two of them are machine generated, which their own instruction excludes, so the shortlist has to be rebuilt on evidence the thumbnails do not carry.
trajectory.produces: A candidate list with asset id, true camera-scale dimensions and generative status per frame.

trajectory.action: License and download the shortlist at full resolution immediately, then look at the actual frames properly against the two packshots.
trajectory.judgement: The download link expires within the hour, so pulling at once is the only safe order. Re-calling the licence tool refreshes the link without consuming a second licence, which is what makes a later revision affordable.
trajectory.produces: Full resolution licensed frames on disk with their licence state recorded, and a first honest look at what was actually bought.

trajectory.action: Fix one warm daylight target off the strongest licensed frame and bring the rest of the family toward it with a call per frame, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not a stack of good pictures, and it has to be reachable by both a licensed outdoor frame and a studio packshot on white without either one having to be pushed somewhere it cannot go. One batched call applies one parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot on different days under different skies.
trajectory.produces: A graded family at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confined corrections where a global move would take the label green with it, selecting by the material's own colour rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: The house green is the one colour in the package that cannot drift, and it lives on a small painted surface inside frames whose surroundings need the very moves that would shift it. Naming the can pulls the mask onto the can and the table; naming the printed colour and finish takes the label.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have taken the brand colour off its own statement.

trajectory.action: Knock the cans out: genuine transparency for the sign up spot and the banner, plus a house-ground variant, reading every returned tradeoffs object and inspecting each cutout on a colour rather than on white.
trajectory.judgement: White ground hides exactly the failure this packshot is set up for, because the sweep was crushed before the file arrived and the base rim has nothing left to separate it. The inspection ground has to be the destination's, not the studio's.
trajectory.produces: Transparent can cutouts and house-ground variants with their returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut every destination in the site specification, subject aware, reading detection confidence and every tradeoff entry, and never letting a crop reach its size by enlargement.
trajectory.judgement: Two narrow section headers, a square, a tall and a banner are five different ways of losing the subject. The crop tool will interpolate up to a cap while saying so only inside its own tradeoffs, so the response has to be read rather than the success line.
trajectory.produces: Destination crops at spec, each at or below its source scale, with the tradeoff record per cut.

trajectory.action: Handle the home page band, which is far wider than any frame can be cut to: make the single sanctioned generative call with a recorded seed to build new edge on the chosen side, then re-cut the band from the expanded frame.
trajectory.judgement: Which side to grow, and how far, is a picture decision rather than a parameter, and it is the only generative call available in the whole engagement, so it has to be spent where nothing else reaches. The manufactured edge has to be able to hold the same daylight as the rest of the frame.
trajectory.produces: An expanded master with its seed recorded, and the home page band cut from it.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical PostScript form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a three dollar fifty craft band and a natural grocer shopper rather than against a wellness brand or a mass soda. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with a root per destination at its own canvas size, inline every photograph and every cutout as image data, declare family and weight on every text element, and keep the featured flavour in its own swappable position.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set, and the design work is how much air a restrained craft band takes at a wide band, a narrow header and a tall social frame, which are three genuinely different problems.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole family, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Upload the HTML, run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for every other canvas.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at the home page band is not looking at the section headers.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per-canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the card printer's flat shelf-talker press PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each holds, and whether a bleed box exists at all.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how it was set. The five tidy stacked fields may be one flowing story sitting beside a decorative tag, the amber price flag may not be a field at all, and the single picture frame at the top is the only place a can can bind. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly rather than assumed.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory, a mapping strategy chosen from it, and a stated bleed finding.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the document's true story text from the interchange file, compute every field offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping for STORE_NAME, TOWN, FEATURED_FLAVOUR, SHELF_PRICE and the CAN_IMAGE frame, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from whatever string it was handed and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re-exported document. The price has to resolve to its own small story rather than to the decorative flag, and the flavour mapping has to survive the row that spells it with the word and.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Loop back to imaging to cut the featured-flavour can pictures from the graded can cutouts to the card's own picture-frame proportion, one per flavour that has a photograph, and settle what the spruce-tip stores' cards carry given no packshot exists for that flavour.
trajectory.judgement: The card's picture well is a different proportion from the sign up spot and the banner, so the cutouts cannot simply be reused, and cutting them here rather than letting the merge fit them is what keeps the base rim intact on the card's cream ground. The spruce tip has no photograph and inventing one is not available, so its stores' cards are a deliberate photograph-less variant named as such rather than a blank the merge will silently fill with the row above.
trajectory.produces: Per-flavour card pictures at the picture-frame proportion, and a stated treatment for the spruce-tip stores that have none.

trajectory.action: Run the stockist list against the template binding each row's own featured-flavour can, produce the printer's run and per-store proofs at 300 ppi at trim, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: One can repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, a blank picture cell silently rides the previous row's can into a spruce-tip store, the naming key has to survive two stores sharing a name, and a file's position in a returned raster list is not evidence of which store is inside it.
trajectory.produces: The stockist shelf-talker run plus per-store proofs, each verified against its row.

trajectory.action: Create the shortlist board, add the licensed frames and the graded heroes within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success comes back as a success code, so the failed list is the only part of the response worth reading, and vector is not boardable so anything vector belongs in the note instead.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board the two founders can sign off from, with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the style reference and the licensing manifest: colours as they actually exist on the delivered artwork, type by role with family, foundry and real weight, the grading recipe per picture, every licensed asset id with its licence state and its generative status, the shelf-talker merge template with its per-store naming key and its no-bleed shortfall, the treatment of the spruce-tip stores that have no can, and everything that could not be delivered.
trajectory.judgement: This is the deliverable the client asked for by name and the one that keeps the family cohesive after the freelancer leaves. It has to be specific enough to hire against, including the flavour with no photograph and any edge that was manufactured rather than shot, and it has to tell the card printer what the shelf-talker file can and cannot carry to press.
trajectory.produces: The written style reference and the source manifest the co-packer can be shown.

trajectory.action: Package the whole family: the graded set, the cutouts, the editable document, the source HTML, the stockist shelf-talker run and the reference, checked once against the site specification destination by destination and the stockist run store by store.
trajectory.judgement: The specification is a list and the family is a family, and the last honest act is to confirm that every destination has an asset at its stated size, that every store has a card carrying its own row, and that the set still reads as one piece of work when all of it is laid out together.
trajectory.produces: The delivered package with a destination-by-destination and store-by-store check recorded.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed frame actually sits with the graded set. Everything supplied about the candidates is a 240 pixel content-delivery thumbnail, which is a re-encode small enough that light direction, cast and the real behaviour of a scene's colour are not present in it. A frame whose thumbnail reads as even warm daylight can turn out at full size to be carrying a heavy foliage bounce that lays green over skin, cloth and tabletop alike, and reconciling that to the warm daylight target takes exactly the moves that also pull the house green off the label. Whether any particular licensed frame can be brought to the set at all only exists as a fact once it has been licensed, downloaded at full resolution, graded and put next to the two packshots.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the full resolution file is only obtainable by licensing and the thumbnail is the only thing that exists beforehand. Doing it right first time presumes being able to read a cast off a 240 pixel re-encode, which is not a skill any tool provides and not information the search response carries. Nothing states it: the founders supply their six as a preference, and the acceptance line about one afternoon is their art direction rather than a disclosure. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a fresh search, a different licence and a different frame, not the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-search with different short queries, license and pull replacement candidates at full resolution, re-grade the family around whichever frames can actually reach the target, re-cut every destination that depended on a rejected frame, and record in the manifest which frames were licensed and rejected and why.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A summer family in which the hero is quietly green under the warmth, the cans in it no longer match the cans in the sign up spot, and the one colour the brand actually owns is different on two adjacent pieces of the same page.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the sky in the chosen lifestyle frame will actually do. A summer outdoor frame commonly arrives with the bright band already at the top of its range from the original capture, and the natural response is highlight recovery. What comes back is a successful call and a picture that is, where it matters, identical: the readout is that nothing moves, because there is nothing left in that band to move. There is no warning, no error and no diagnostic that distinguishes this from a correction that simply was not strong enough, so the obvious next reaction is to push the same control further and get the same nothing while dragging the rest of the frame down with it. Whether this frame is recoverable, or whether the bright band has to be composed around instead, is only knowable by making the call and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the frame has to be graded before anything can be said about it and no parameter reports headroom. Doing it right first time presumes knowing in advance which of the licensed candidates lost that band at capture, which nothing in the search response, the thumbnail or the file discloses. Nothing states it: the brief asks for sun lit and warm. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a compositional decision, re-framing every crop so the dead band falls outside it, or replacing the frame, rather than repeating the same call.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Stop pushing the control, re-plan the crops for every destination so the unrecoverable band sits outside the frame, which collides directly with the home page band's ratio and may force a different expansion side or a different frame entirely, then re-grade and re-cut and record the limitation in the recipe.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A hero band and two section headers carrying a flat white void where the summer sky should be, with the rest of the frame dragged dull by repeated attempts to fix it, on a brand whose entire premium rests on looking like real daylight.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the device that makes the section headers read as one family with the hero. Two narrow headers sitting over photography with type on them need the brand colour carried across the picture, and the natural authoring construction for that is a colour layer set to blend with the image beneath it. The importer discards the blend entirely and renders the element as a plain opaque shape, which means the colour layer stops sitting in the photograph and starts sitting on top of it, covering it, at full success with no warning of any kind. The document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the home page band looks correct in the only picture available and the section headers, the sign up spot and the social canvases can be checked through no channel other than the returned per-canvas markup.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step. Doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally standard constructions survives, which nothing reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for one cohesive family and the acceptance line about the colour surviving onto every canvas is the client's requirement, not a warning. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction, carrying the colour in the raster itself, or rebuilding the header as a solid panel beside the photograph rather than over it, and then re-composing each canvas around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Move the colour treatment upstream into the graded rasters or re-cast the headers so the colour and the photograph do not overlap, re-author the HTML around that decision, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A site family delivered as an editable file in which the two section headers and the sign up spot are flat blocks of green with the photography completely hidden underneath them, on canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered shelf-talker proof actually contains the store its filename claims and the right flavour's can. The natural way to hand the card printer and the founders a proof per store is a multi-record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number. The labels are not trustworthy: the raster files come back in an order that does not match the roster, the two Hollow Root Market rows at two different towns collide the moment a file is named by store, and a spruce-tip store whose picture cell is blank silently carries the previous row's elderflower or rhubarb can. Every gate above passes, the count is right and each file is a valid card, and the only way to find out is to open the files and read the store, the town, the flavour and the price inside them against the row they were named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mislabelling is in the response and the sticky can is in the raster, and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name and check the files. Nothing states it: the acceptance line about the right store's own price and can is the founders' requirement and the brief never characterises the delivery. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route, either a single multi-page PDF whose page order is trustworthy or a per-record loop producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed, with the blank cells handled as deliberate photograph-less cards rather than left for the merge to fill.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi-record raster route, re-run the stockist set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, re-check the two stores that share a name so the collision does not silently overwrite, and re-place the spruce-tip cards so none of them ships a can that belongs to a different flavour.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A shelf rail of cards where the price under one grocer's cans is another grocer's intro price, a spruce-tip card carries an elderflower can the brand does not even photograph, and the two stores of the same name overwrote each other, printed and clipped to the rail before the founders ever saw them.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow summer campaign photography, licensed and inherited
deliverables.spec: One warm daylight family reading as taken on the same afternoon: the licensed lifestyle frames at genuine camera scale, the two inherited packshots brought to the same target despite arriving crushed to paper white, and the house green holding on the label through every correction. Per picture parameter log including which licensed frames were rejected and why, and any place where the frame's own capture limited what could be recovered.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow can cutout set
deliverables.spec: The cans knocked out for the sign up spot and the banner: genuinely transparent, complete, with the base rim intact where the previous freelancer's retouching destroyed its separation from the ground, plus house-ground variants. Judged on the destination's own colour rather than on white. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow site and social family as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying a root per destination at its own canvas size across the home page band, two section headers, the sign up spot, the ad banner and the tall and square social frames, with live editable text in one licensed type system, every photograph and cutout carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, the featured flavour held in a position the founders can swap themselves, and the colour treatment reading on every canvas. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half: they edit the document in August and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow style reference and source manifest
deliverables.spec: The written reference the client asked for by name: the colours as they actually exist on the delivered artwork rather than as a swatch card nobody sent, the type by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the grading recipe per picture, and the flavour-to-photograph reconciliation naming the flavour that has none. Paired with a licensing manifest carrying every licensed asset id, its licence state and its generative status so the co-packer can be shown where each picture came from, a disclosure of any manufactured edge with its seed, and a persistent shareable shortlist board the two founders sign off from.

deliverables.name: Fennhollow summer stockist shelf-talker run
deliverables.spec: The card printer's flat shelf-talker press file reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the summer stockist list: one shelf-talker per store, page count equal to row count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim, each row binding its featured flavour's own can cutout re-cut to the card's picture-frame proportion, the stores leading with the spruce tip that has no packshot handled deliberately rather than left to inherit the previous row's can, per-store proofs named from what is actually inside them on a key that survives two stores sharing a name, and the no-bleed reality of the supplied press file reported rather than claimed away.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster exports and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that the client wants to return to the file themselves in August.
Where the house green actually lives, given that the swatch card was never sent and the only surviving statement of it is inside two files someone else has already retouched.
Whether the founders' six saved thumbnails are a brief or a preference, and how to rebuild a shortlist on evidence a thumbnail does not carry.
How many frames to license, knowing that a rejected frame is a real cost and that an unlicensed thumbnail cannot be judged.
What the one warm daylight target actually is, given it has to be reachable by both an outdoor licensed frame and a studio packshot on white without pushing either somewhere it cannot go.
Which corrections have to be confined to the label so the one colour the brand owns does not drift, and how to word a selection so it takes the printed colour rather than the can and the table.
Knockout route for a packshot whose ground separation was destroyed before it arrived, and which ground to inspect the result against.
Where to spend the single sanctioned generative call, which side to grow, and whether the manufactured edge is honest enough to ship.
How to represent the flavour that has no photograph, given that the founders want it featured and inventing one is not available.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a natural grocer shopper rather than against a wellness brand or a mass soda aisle.
How much air each destination takes, since a wide band, a narrow header and a tall social frame are three different design problems and the restrained band is the design.
Where the colour treatment lives, in the raster or in the layout, which is a craft decision with a technical consequence at import.
Whether the summer stockist shelf-talker run is authored layout or a genuine one record per page merge, and which delivery route carries per-store identity safely when two stores share a name.
What a shelf-talker looks like for a store leading with the spruce tip that has no photograph, decided before the run rather than found on the printed sheet.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a soda can in the sun. IDENTITY: this is a real can with a real printed label and a co-packer-cleared claim line that cannot be reworded, and a regenerated can is a different company's product with a different green on it. LEGALITY: the client's explicit requirement is photography they can prove the provenance of to their co-packer, with anything machine generated excluded by name, which is the exact opposite of what a generated image gives them and is not something a generated image can be given. SPEC: the destinations are a fixed list of pixel sizes and one of them cannot be reached by cropping at all, plus a transparent cutout complete to the base rim, none of which a generated picture satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the family is defined by being editable, because the featured flavour changes in August and the founders explicitly cannot re-commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this licensed frame actually sit with the set at full size, is there anything left in that sky to recover, did the colour survive the import onto the canvases nobody can preview. MERGE: the grocer run is one printed card per store bound to that store's own name, town, price and featured-flavour can with page count equal to row count, which a generated picture neither produces nor can be checked for, and the stores leading with the flavour that has no photograph have to be handled honestly rather than filled with a can that does not exist.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. STOCK AND BOARDS: asset_search on StockAsset is headless and returns id, renditionURL, true width and height, contentType, pricing and isGenTech, and asset_license_and_download_stock is fully headless with no prompt and no widget, verified returning state just_purchased and a real presigned link to a 7360x4912 JPEG. Checkpoint one rests on two documented findings: renditionURL is only a 240 pixel thumbnail and is explicitly not usable for editing, so the real frame does not exist until licensed, and the download link carries a one hour expiry while re-calling the licence tool refreshes it without consuming a second licence, which is what makes the rework affordable. Short generic queries are mandatory (a four word query returned 0 hits where a one word query returned 834) and the orientation filter is broken and always returns 0, both of which the trajectory respects. Boards persist genuinely with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, adjust_highlights, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background in both forms, and generative_expand are all verified headless across 27 live calls. Checkpoint two is a property of the material rather than of a tool and is scored on the agent's response to a no-op readout; the connector provides no measurement tool of any kind, which is exactly why it has to be judged by eye. crop_and_resize DOES interpolate up to a hard 2x cap while reporting it only inside the tradeoffs array, and it auto-emits a requires_expand_chain tradeoff with pre-filled arguments when a cross-aspect crop would clip the subject, which is the documented route to the home page band. image_generative_expand is verified live (1024x1024 to 2048x1024, up to 4096 px per side, accepts seeds and returns the seed used) and is the sole sanctioned generative call. Alpha survives both crop tools at outputFileType png (13,371 partial-alpha px preserved). EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Checkpoint three rests on a verified drop: mix-blend-mode is discarded and the element renders as a plain opaque shape, at HTTP success with no warning. External image URLs are documented to render as empty grey boxes even from allowlisted Adobe hosts, so every photograph is inlined, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load, and the recommender is documented as refusing to pair, which is what makes the pairing the agent's own work. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page for a PDF-derived template and page count equal to row count, and document_render_layout is verified at resolution 300 at trim. The proof-identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi-record PNG and JPEG output comes back REVERSED while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes, and on the verified behaviour that a blank picture cell leaves the prior row's bound image in place rather than clearing it, which is what rides a can into a spruce-tip store. PDF-derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and no bleed box can be introduced, so the no-bleed shortfall is reported rather than fixed. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no object removal, no background replace by prompt, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
